title: Grafana
subtitle: Dashboards are how I captured the numbers on this site.

stats.label: hidden-state extractions in a single test run

lede: Inference Fabric made claims about GPU efficiency that I wanted to prove from a screen, so I built its dashboards around the measures that justify the design. The panels show tokens per second split into prefill and decode, padding waste, shape switches, key-value cache hit rate, the broker's lanes and cold tier, probes and extractions per second, and a token-accounting difference that should always read zero. I chart domain measures first, because padding waste and token-accounting drift say more about a GPU pipeline than host load does, and I built each fabric dashboard alongside the feature it measured, so a change was visible the day it landed. Every fabric figure on this site comes from these panels.
quote: I decide what to measure as part of the design, and I build the instruments that let me defend each number.
evidence: Observability and alerting: dashboards built around domain measures, ~137 broker metrics on 31 panels, file-based target discovery and Alertmanager routing to SMS.
GPU pipeline metrics: tokens per second, padding waste, cache hit rate and a token-accounting difference that reads zero, with 163,000 tokens per second read from the panels.
Cost attribution for AI work: per-seat cost and cache reuse for a work order read from PostgreSQL rollups, cache reuse spanning 43% to 97% across seats.
author: Corey James
